summary: The run built a strong damage-and-scaling Ironclad deck, but its HP declined steadily and it reached Act 2 fights with little margin for error. The decisive failure was the final Cultist combat, where early setup consumed the opening turns without removing an enemy or creating block, leaving the player at 12/80 HP before meaningful stabilization.

lessons.title: Add defensive utility before taking more offensive scaling
lessons.situation: When HP is trending downward and reward choices offer block, exhaust, or defensive utility alongside another damage or scaling card, prioritize the defensive option unless the deck has a clear immediate need for damage.
lessons.lesson: Do not repeatedly add offensive enablers without increasing defensive reliability. The final deck had four starter Defends and only one additional permanent block card, Power Through, despite several opportunities involving Power Through, True Grit, or Sentinel.
evidence_points: At Act 1 Floor 1, Spot Weakness was chosen over Power Through.
At Act 1 Floor 5, Dual Wield, Dropkick, and Warcry were skipped; at Act 1 Floor 14, Body Slam, Sentinel, and Wild Strike were skipped.

The final 18-card deck contained four Defends and Power Through as its only added block card, alongside Spot Weakness+, Sword Boomerang, Thunderclap, Rampage, Double Tap, Limit Break, Seeing Red, and Heavy Blade.
lessons.reasoning: The reward history shows repeated additions of damage or scaling while the final deck gained only one non-starter block card. Since HP fell from 75/80 at Act 1 Floor 5 to 40/80 at Floor 14 and 30/80 before the final fight, future rewards should place greater value on defensive utility when available.

lessons.title: Do not spend a low-HP opening turn on setup without immediate control
lessons.situation: When entering a multi-enemy fight at low HP and several enemies can attack, use opening energy to kill, heavily damage, or block against a concrete threat rather than chaining setup cards that leave the board largely intact.
lessons.lesson: Sequence cards such as Seeing Red, Double Tap, and Spot Weakness around an immediate survival or kill breakpoint. If setup does not remove an enemy or provide mitigation, reassess before ending the turn with no block.
evidence_points: The final fight began at 30/80 HP with three Cultists alive and 0 block.
On Turn 1, Seeing Red, Double Tap, and one Strike were played, then the turn ended with all three Cultists still alive and no player block.
By Turn 3, the player was at 12/80 HP; Power Through and Defend were then played while two attacking Cultists remained.
lessons.reasoning: The logged sequence shows that the opening setup did not produce immediate board control or defense, allowing the attack cycle to reduce HP from 30 to 12 before defensive cards were used. In similar situations, the opening hand should be evaluated against the next incoming attack rather than assuming setup is safe.

lessons.title: Use healing earlier when repeated fights are consuming the HP buffer
lessons.situation: At a campfire after several damaging combats, especially when entering the next segment below roughly half health, choose healing when the remaining HP buffer is unlikely to cover multiple upcoming fights.
lessons.lesson: Keep smithing at high HP, but switch to rest sooner once combat damage is accumulating. An upgrade is less valuable than preserving enough HP to survive the next sequence of fights and reach later campfires or bosses safely.
evidence_points: The player smith-ed Bash at 75/80 HP on Act 1 Floor 6 and Spot Weakness at 73/80 on Floor 8.
After HP fell to 40/80, the player rested at Act 1 Floor 15.
The run still reached Act 2 Floor 18 at 41/80 HP, Floor 20 at 30/80 HP, and the final combat at 30/80 HP.
lessons.reasoning: The early upgrades were taken with a substantial HP buffer, but the later rest did not prevent the run from entering Act 2 with limited survivability. Future campfire decisions should account for cumulative damage across the upcoming fights, not just the value of one additional upgrade.
